newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada has first year profit since '89.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada has first year profit since '89.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, which earlier this week won a C$1.4 billion takeover bid for Britain's Clyde Petroleum Plc, on Thursday reported its first annual profit since 1989.

Gulf Canada, which has undergone a massive restructuring since Texas oilman J.P. Bryan took the helm as chief executive in 1995, rang up earnings for 1996 of C$37 million or C$0.03 per share, up from a 1995 loss of C$28 million or C$0.32 per share.
Cash flow grew to C$440 million or C$1.72 per share, up from C$292 million or C$1.17 per share the year before.
"We are entering a period of step-change for Gulf and in 1997 we will become truly international in scope," Bryan said in a statement.
Gulf said higher production volumes and commodity prices more than compensated for higher operating costs during the year.
The company said higher cash flow was mostly reinvested in capital and exploration expenditures, which rose to C$644 million from C$502 million in 1995.
The funds were used to participate in over 500 wells during the year, with a success rate of 73 per cent for completed wells, Gulf said.

Most were drilled in western Canada, but Gulf also participated in a number of so-called "big hit" opportunities that resulted in large gas discoveries at Sumpal and Bungkal in South Sumatra, it said.

Gulf's average daily sales for 1996 climbed to 131,300 barrels of oil equivalent per day with oil and gas liquids sales increasing 11 percent to 87,200 barrels per day and natural gas sales rising 40 percent to 441 million cubic feet per day.
The company sold C$278 million of assets in 1996, including a number of higher operating cost properties sold at the end of the year, it said.
Most of the proceeds financed the mid-year acquisition of Pennzoil Co Canadian assets, Gulf said.

The company said its oil and liquids reserves grew to 392 million barrels at the end of 1996 from 377 million the year before. Natural gas reserves increased to nearly 2 trillion cubic feet from 1.4 TCF in 1995.
